issue: Under Payton v. New York, must officers have probable cause to believe an arrestee is inside a home before entering without a search warrant, or does 'reason to believe' require something less?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. IV; Payton v. New York, 445 U.S. 573, 603 (1980)

sides.position: 'Reason to believe' under Payton embodies the same standard of reasonableness as probable cause.
cases: United States v. Gorman, 314 F.3d 1105, 1112 (9th Cir. 2002)

sides.position: 'Reason to believe' under Payton means something less than probable cause.
cases: Valdez v. McPheters, 172 F.3d 1220, 1224–25, 1227 n.5 (10th Cir. 1999)

quote: However, there is a circuit split over the meaning of “reason to believe” under Payton.
cite: United States v. Maley, No. 20-2073 (10th Cir. 2021)
